Built to evaluate and improve agent capabilities for supporting legal work

Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) was created to evaluate agents on the real work of lawyers at law firms and in-house legal teams. The tasks require agents to work through a full client matter, decide which documents matter, and produce finished work products such as memos, redlines, and filings.

LAB was built in three steps. First, practicing lawyers broke real client matters into the tasks a partner would give an associate. Second, they wrote expert rubrics that reflect what a partner or client would check. Third, agents ran each task in a sandbox with the matter files, and a task passes only if every rubric criterion passes.

There are 1,749 tasks in LAB across 24 practice areas and in-house contracting, graded by more than 100,000 rubric criteria. The full LAB dataset is available open-source, along with Harvey's execution harness for running and scoring agents.

Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) is an open-source benchmark that tests whether AI agents can complete long, multi-step legal work. Harvey built it. Each task has an instruction, a client matter with the relevant documents, and a required work product, such as a memo, redline, issues list, or filing. Expert rubrics grade that work product.

Harvey built LAB from real client matters handled by practicing lawyers. The team split each matter into the separate tasks a partner would normally give an associate. Practicing attorneys wrote the rubrics to reflect what a supervising partner or client would check before the work goes out.

Earlier legal benchmarks, such as LegalBench, CUAD, LEXam, and Harvey's own BigLaw Bench, test short-horizon reasoning: read a contract and answer a question, or compare two cases. LAB tests long-horizon work. The agent has to search a full client matter, decide what's relevant, and produce a finished deliverable.

They measure different things. APEX-Agents, developed in collaboration with Harvey and Box, tests agents across three professional services jobs (corporate lawyer, investment banking analyst, and management consultant) using multiple applications. Harvey LAB goes deep on legal work only, with 1,749 tasks across 24 practice areas and in-house contracting.
Built to evaluate and improve agent capabilities for physical engineering work

Physical-Engineering's Last Exam (PLE) was created to evaluate agents on the real work of mechanical, electrical, civil, and structural engineers. The tasks require agents to work through a full project folder, find the governing codes and physical limits, and produce deliverables a licensed reviewer would sign off on.

PLE was built two ways. For expert-authored tasks, practicing engineers created the project folders, prompts, and grading rubrics from scratch. For co-authored tasks, engineers designed the task, an agent pipeline assembled the environment and grader, and the engineers validated every task and made it harder. An agent earns optimization points only if its design passes every hard safety check.

Physical-Engineering's Last Exam (PLE) is a benchmark and open competition that tests whether AI agents can complete long, end-to-end physical engineering work. Google built it in collaboration with Mercor. Each task has a prompt, a project folder with the relevant files, and required production deliverables. Grading tools check those deliverables for code compliance and cost efficiency.

Frontier models now score above 90% on many academic benchmarks, which mostly test textbook question answering, single tool calls, or small, self-contained design problems. PLE tests long-horizon work. The agent has to search a full project folder, decide what's relevant, and produce safe, code-compliant, and cost-effective designs.

The benchmark comprises ~700 interconnected policy documents (≈195K tokens) across 21 product categories, from product selection to dispute resolution to account management. Agents are graded against backend database state outcomes, such as whether a dispute was actually filed, a credit issue resolved, or an account opened correctly, rather than matching reference answers.

Example tasks include cash-back card recommendations, dispute resolution with competing policies, and business account selection with conflicting promotions. The benchmark was published in collaboration with Sierra AI and includes an open-source dataset and execution harness.

The Revenue Per Employee Breakdown
Revenue scales with headcount
Contractors aren’t employees (they’re “managed” talent)
Revenue scales with contractor base, not core headcount
Mercor’s contractors are their product, not their employees.
When OpenAI pays Mercor for 1,000 hours of expert training time, that revenue counts against Mercor’s ~50 core employees—not the hundreds of contractors who performed the work.
It’s a brilliant arbitrage of the revenue-per-employee metric.
Mercor’s client list is essentially the AI lab oligopoly. If OpenAI or Anthropic decides to build in-house training capabilities, Mercor’s revenue could evaporate quickly.
How contractor classification rules evolve could impact Mercor’s business model. If those 30,000 contractors were reclassified as employees, the economics change dramatically.
The company reportedly told investors they’re on track to hit $500M ARR faster than Cursor achieved it—which would make them the fastest-growing enterprise AI startup in history.

At $4.5 million in revenue per employee, they’re more efficient than any tech giant. At $10 billion valuation, they’re more valuable than companies 10x their age. At 22 years old, their founders have achieved what most entrepreneurs dream about for decades.
Why is Mercor’s revenue per employee so high?
Their 30,000+ contractors aren’t employees—they’re “managed talent.” Revenue from contractor hours counts against Mercor’s small core team of ~50 employees.

Mercor、1日200万ドル超を支払うAI人材基盤へ 急成長で見えた自動化の条件

AI人材プラットフォームのMercorは、世界3万人超の週次アクティブな契約人材に対し、1日200万ドル超を支払う規模まで急拡大した。急成長の裏側では、手作業の決済、分散したデータ、監査・承認プロセスが事業拡大の制約となり、決済基盤を全面的に再設計している。人材ビジネスにおいてAIエージェントによる業務自動化を進めるには、AI導入以前に「正しいデータ」と「統制可能な業務基盤」を作る必要があることを示す事例だ。
米国のAI人材プラットフォームMercorが、急成長に伴い決済・請求インフラを大幅に再設計している。同社によれば、事業開始から17カ月で年間換算売上5億ドル規模に到達し、2026年には10億ドルを突破。世界3万人超の週次アクティブ契約人材に対する支払いは、現在1日200万ドルを超えている。
MercorはAI企業や大手企業と専門人材をつなぐ二面市場型のプラットフォームを運営する。企業への請求と、複数国・複数通貨にまたがる契約人材への支払いを同時に処理するため、契約、稼働管理、価格計算、請求、支払い、会計処理までを一貫して管理する必要がある。
しかし、取引量が週20万ドルから1,400万ドル超へ増える過程で、スタートアップ初期の運用が限界を迎えた。例えば毎週の支払い処理では、SQLによる確認、複数決済事業者との照合、資金残高確認、担当者による承認などが積み重なり、週10時間超のエンジニア工数が発生していた。
そこでMercorは、決済データを後から書き換える方式から、すべての金融イベントを履歴として残す「追記型の不変台帳」へ移行。支払い状態も「発生→承認→支払可能→支払済→取消」という統一された状態管理に整理している。
さらに、タスク完了情報や契約データも統一し、支払い処理の完全自動化を進める。AIエージェントが支払いなどを実行する場合にも、取引前に監査記録を作成し、一定金額を超えれば人間の承認を要求する仕組みを採用した。

Mercorとは？海外AI案件で外貨建て報酬を得る選択肢と確認すべき条件

外貨を得る方法は、投資や為替取引だけではありません。海外のプロジェクトへ専門知識や作業を提供し、その対価として外貨建ての報酬を受け取る働き方もあります。Mercorは、その選択肢の一つになり得る海外人材プラットフォームです。ただし、すべての案件がドル建てでも、Wiseで受け取れるわけでもありません。採用、案件量、報酬額、継続、受取通貨は保証されず、募集と契約の最新条件を一件ずつ確認する必要があります。
この記事では「MercorとはどんなAIリモートワークサービスか」を、海外案件と外貨受け取りの実務面から整理します。目立つ報酬表示だけで判断せず、仕事の内容、契約、支払い、税務まで確認するための順番を解説します。
Mercorは専門性とAIプロジェクトをつなぐ場
Mercorは、専門知識や実務経験を持つ人と、AIモデルの評価・改善・学習支援などのプロジェクトをつなぐプラットフォームです。仕事には、AIが生成した文章を品質基準に沿って評価する、専門分野の内容をレビューする、調査結果を検証する、文章を改善するといった業務が含まれる場合があります。
海外クライアントへ自分で営業する一般的な受託とは違い、掲載された募集に応募し、案件ごとの選考やアセスメントを受ける形が中心です。登録しただけで仕事が割り当てられるわけではありません。地域、経験、言語、稼働時間などの条件が合い、選考を通過して初めて契約へ進む可能性があります。
